measured_run.note: Durations of the `race this group` STEP, read with scripts/race-full-report.sh. modules-rest died at its ceiling (45.2 min of 45) and was split for that reason. ⛔ The provenance is cited WITHOUT repository or run id: this file SHIPS in the published tree, and a private repository name there is a leak — the export's leak gate stopped it, not a review. ⛔ And modules-sessions later moved to its own job: it exhausted the 35 min `-timeout` inside modules-rest (2,100 s). Its figure here is the CEILING it consumed, not its real duration — the real one is unknown because the clock cut it, and that is why it cannot be used for balancing yet.

parallel_why: ⛔ `go test`'s `-parallel` inherits GOMAXPROCS, and since Go 1.25 GOMAXPROCS comes from the cgroup QUOTA, not from the visible CPUs. Measured on one development host: NumCPU 16, quota 6, GOMAXPROCS 6 — and the dump showed EXACTLY 6 parent tests running. On the runner TWO were running, so its effective quota is 2, not the advertised 4 vCPU. With 730 tests that call t.Parallel() and wait on timers and I/O, two slots turn a package of minutes into one that does not fit in 35. `parallel` decouples TEST concurrency from the CPU quota, which is the right thing when what the tests wait for is not CPU. 0 = do not pass the flag.
